lines.en: label christmalloween2:
scene tsukiokamalloween3

: You see, Chinami, the key benefit of unlimited PTO is that it provides the illusion of employee-centric viewpoints without actually sacrificing anything and ultimately having the reverse effect on your minions. I mean staff.
: Once you bring a finite amount into play, people feel incentivized to make use of it and actually take more vacation days than they would without any sort of maximum at all.
: Chinami thinks it would be good for employee acquisition as well. She will take it up with our shareholders during the Q4 earnings report.
scene tsukiokamalloween2
: It appears that our monthly meeting has adjourned then! Excellent work today as always.
: Thanks, Tsukasa! Chinami can’t help but wonder how our friends and family will react when they find out we bought Microsoft, though.
: We’ll keep it a secret for now so they keep treating us like kids. But one day, when they least expect it, boom! We’re actually even wealthier than they are!
: Chinami’s family isn’t wealthy at all! But she still understands what Tsukasa means.
scene tsukiokamalloween3
: When are you going to stop referring to yourself in the third person? You know I won’t tell anybody if you talk normally.
: When is Tsukasa going to start referring to Tsukasa in the third person because it’s more fun?
: Tsukasa doesn’t think so.
scene tsukiokamalloween4
: Oh. Actually, that was kind of fun.
: See? Chinami is worried Tsukasa’s mom might think Tsukasa has some sort of degenerative brain disease if she starts doing that now, though.
scene tsukiokamalloween5
: But maybe that’s a good idea?! She’ll feel way worse about making you marry some old guy if your brain is dying!
: I thought we agreed to not talk about that today in the spirit of Christmalloween?
: If Tsukasa is going to talk to Chinami about sex all the time now, Chinami thinks it’s only fair that Chinami gets to talk about things she wants too. Even if they violate notarized agreements.
scene tsukiokamalloween6
: Fine. Then I suppose it can not be helped. Especially since you have acquired information I am inclined and motivated to trade for.
: For the millionth time, Chinami doesn’t want to talk about her watching her big sister and Papa turn into rabid sex animals.
: Then I will have to do this the old fashioned way. By installing hidden cameras throughout your property while you are away so I can watch them on my own.
scene tsukiokamalloween7
: What kind of “old fashioned way” is that?! Keep your cameras out of Chinami’s house! She doesn’t want you peeping on her! Her days being numbered makes them stressful enough as is!
scene tsukiokamalloween8
: Why don’t you just stop being sick? Is there really no cure?
: Chinami isn’t technically sick at all. Her body just makes her get sick really easily. That’s why she showed up today wearing a dog helmet.
: And probably why the cleaning crew was working overtime. I’m just kind of confused about how we can help mom’s cancer-friend but not you. Your thing seems way less serious than that.
: Chinami doesn’t really understand either. But at least she doesn’t have a degenerative brain disease like Tsukasa.
: If you only had a day left to live, what do you think you’d do?
scene tsukiokamalloween9
: So dark! Chinami doesn’t like that question!
: Really? I figured you’d already have an answer for it if your days really are numbered.
: Well I- she doesn’t! Chinami! Me! Bad Tsukasa! Go to your room!
scene tsukiokamalloween10
: Fine. But you’re coming with me. For I have learned of a place called the “dark web” that is immune to all forms of parental control!
: Aaaaaaaahhhhhhhhh!
scene tsukiokamalloween11
: Chinami, darling — please don’t scream like that. You’ll work yourself up and I don’t want you going home all weak and exhausted, okay?
: Okay, Mrs. Tsukioka! I’m so glad that I have Tsukasa here to help me feel better! Who knows what would happen if she was suddenly gone? I’d probably just die!
scene tsukiokamalloween12
: Right...I’m sure that is exactly what would happen.
: Codependency seems to run in that family. So I’m not entirely sure if that statement is as inaccurate as you subtly seem to be implying, Mother.
scene tsukiokamalloween13
: Oh? Is that a hint of sourness I detect in your voice, Touka? Has Chika’s attachment to your beloved teacher finally taken its toll on you?
: He is not my beloved anything. Nor is he even my teacher at this point in time. That role has been inherited by someone who actually cares about my education.
: Arakawa-Sensei would care as well if you’d only let him teach you the area in which he excels instead of throwing temper tantrums over it.
scene tsukiokamalloween14
: If you’re insisting that my reluctance to let a grown man teach my younger sister about sex is a “tantrum,” then perhaps our viewpoints on the matter are simply incompatible.
: I’m inclined to believe that was merely me acting as a rational human being instead of whatever you’re slowly turning into, though.
: A caring mother, of course. I only want what’s best for my girls.
scene tsukiokamalloween15
: Right. And I suppose it’s best for Tsukasa to be pawned off on whatever brand of perverted predator would actually betroth himself to a child.
: She’s not much younger than you, Touka. Do you really believe a few years makes that much of a difference?
scene tsukiokamalloween16
: Yes, actually. Which is why I also have no qualms with asking you to stay out of that aspect of my life and focus instead on those where your opinion is wanted.
: You’ve gotten quite good at standing up to me, darling. I knew sending you off on your own would change you, but I’d be lying if I said I expected it to be this drastic.
: I’m not changing at all. I’m just noticing things I never had before.
: Oh, you’re changing. But love can do that to a person. Just like how love is what turned me into the woman you suddenly have so many issues with.
scene tsukiokamalloween17
: If this love you speak of is for your children, you certainly have an odd way of showing it.
: It’ll make more sense when my time has come and gone and you sit atop the throne this family has built.
: But, in the meantime, perhaps you should just trust me? I haven’t led you astray so far, have I?
: Astray? No. Just into the arms and sights of a man who could ruin my life at any moment.
: His arms, you say?
: It was a figure of speech, Mother. He’s yet to lay a finger on me.
: He has a surprising amount of willpower when he really applies himself, doesn’t he?
: Yes. I just struggle to understand why he only exercises such restraint with me when I am twice the woman any of those girls could ever hope to be.
: Given what he said to you in the past, I imagine he just has a very strange relationship with mothers.
: Don’t we all?
: The fortunate ones, maybe. Or unfortunate depending on the circumstances. For I know you’ve abhorred me lately, but you still respect me. Isn’t that right?
scene tsukiokamalloween18
: Hah...
: I don’t abhor you, Mother. I just don’t understand you as well as I thought I did. And that is...extremely irritating to me as it ultimately results in me questioning my actions and choices.
: I know there’s a method to this madness. You wouldn’t be here today if that were not the case.
: But without an understanding of what that madness is, I struggle to perceive it as anything else at all.
: Especially when I’m learning every day that there may be more to all of this place than I initially believed.
: Oh? Is this gossip I hear? Spill the tea, Touka. Have you heard that phrase before? Tea? How fun. You young people have the most curious vernacular.
: Mother, I have a question that is going to sound insane.
: And I ask that you simply answer yes or no, but I imagine you will not honor that request as most questions can not be fully answered in such a way.
: Oh? Well, let’s hear it then. It seems rather serious based on your tone.
: Is the body of my classmate’s mother buried beneath the everblooming sakura?
scene tsukiokamalloween19
: Why, that does sound insane. Pray tell, where did you get that idea?
: A reliable source. One who knows far more about...basically everything than anyone I’ve ever encountered.
: Even this family?
: No...They’d have no way of knowing anything that goes on here as even I do not yet understand everything that occurs within these walls.
: But there’s a poem she showed me that...very well could be naught more than flowery symbolism both literally and figuratively that...
: Well, it sounded like it was talking about our tree. And combined with your interest in both Sensei and the seemingly omniscient knowledge of this classmate-
: You believe her.
: I...can not refute her. Not nearly as much as I want to at least. For this claim sounds so extremely bizarre, but...so specific that it provides the illusion of merit even if none actually exists.
: And the classmate that raised this concern to you is Nodoka Nagasawa, I presume?
scene tsukiokamalloween20
: Yes, but...how did you-
: I’d be foolish not to know the name of the girl who's been consistenly upstaging you in every single academic field through two different schools now.
: Excellent writer as well. Have you picked up “The Light of Last Summer” yet? Excellent read. Quite relevant to your...situation too.
scene tsukiokamalloween21
: Curious businesswoman, though. It takes a very odd mind to conceptualize and subsequently invent a four-sided sex toy.
: I...know little of such a device. But yes. That is the girl I’m referring to. But the classmate whose mother is thought to be buried beneath our tree is-
: None other than your teacher’s very own niece-turned-daughter, Ami Arakawa.
scene tsukiokamalloween22
: Correct?
: It’s true then?
scene tsukiokamalloween23
: Now, I never said that. There are just very few girls in your class with dead mothers linked directly to poetry.
: This is why I wanted a yes or a no. Complicating the answer is just going to make me even more confused.
: Well, let me ask you a question then. For what reason would we bury the body of some woman beneath a tree?
scene tsukiokamalloween24
: I can’t even completely discern your motivations for having Sensei become Tsukasa’s sex-tutor yet and you expect me to figure out the answer to that?!
: I don’t know! You do weird things sometimes! This could very well be one of those!
: There’s no need to yell, dear. I don’t want you getting exhausted either.
scene tsukiokamalloween25
: There’s no one buried beneath the tree. And there’s no need for you to concern yourself with it when there are much bigger things out there you must be worrying about instead.
: Like...what?
: Yourself. Your friendships. Your relationships. Things that will advance both your life and your career.
: If we honored or delved into every single rumor about our family, we’d never get anything done. So the best course of action, more often than not, is to simply ignore them.
: And if you’re lying to me?...
: Then I’m lying for a reason.
scene tsukiokamalloween26
: But I suppose that could be a lie as well, couldn’t it?
: Quite the paradox, don’t you think?
: I don’t...really know what to think anymore...
scene black
: Then take that as your sign to stop thinking about it at all. We’re far too important to worry about things like gardening. We have workers for that.
: I...suppose that is true. And that someone would have likely...already uncovered such a thing if it were actually there...
: Exactly. Now, why don’t we get back to enjoying ourselves? You skipped out on your Christmas party to be with me this year, didn’t you?
: Yes, but-
: Wait, Christmas? What’s-
: Ah! Silly me. Christmalloween, I mean. That’s enough wine for me tonight.
: Uhh...okay. But-
: Actually, on second thought, why don’t you buzz in one of the butlers? I’d like you to get a taste of the Château Mouton Rothschild that came in this morning. And one more glass won’t kill me.
scene tsukiokamalloween27
: So you like really saw them doing it? Up close?
: Why are we talking about this again?! Chinami thought we escaped that topic!
: I can’t help it, okay?! First, he did it in front of me. Then he did it in front of you! Pattern recognition, Chinami! He could be doing this on purpose to show us!
scene tsukiokamalloween28
: Chinami doesn’t think so...She was asleep when it happened and...big sis Chika wasn’t even home yet when Papa fell asleep too, so...
: She...She thinks this time was just a coincidence...
: Or Jeeves is actually a lolicon!
scene tsukiokamalloween29
: Chinami acknowledges the possibility of this and is suddenly more reluctant to invite Papa into the bath with her. Things are too real now.
scene tsukiokamalloween30
: Taking a bath with him is such a good way to find out, though!
: Find out what?! How to cross a line we’d need to move to Alabama just to live with?!
: Where is Alabama?!
: I don’t know! I’ve just heard that this would be normal there!
scene tsukiokamalloween31
: Chinami, you have a real chance to make a scientific breakthrough here.
: Chinami doesn’t want to make a scientific breakthrough here! She doesn’t look at her papa that way! How many times does she have to tell you that?!
: You don’t need to do anything! You just need to find out if his penis gets hard or not. Because if it does, it means-
scene tsukiokamalloween32
: Chinami knows what it means! And if Tsukasa is so desperate to make a scientific breakthrough, maybe she should be the one to do it!
scene tsukiokamalloween33
: Fine! Then maybe I will!
: Good!
: Yeah! It is good! Coward!
: Pervert!
scene tsukiokamalloween34
: Mngh...
: Hmmf...
scene tsukiokamalloween35
: So, like...did you see how big it was?
: Huge. Big sis Chika must be the strongest girl in the world.
scene black
: How huge? Show me with your hands.
: Like, um...uhh...this?
: What? No way. You’re lying. That’s physically impossible. The human body can’t fit more than like four inches inside, max. That’s an undisputed fact.
: Or maybe it was...more like this?
: That’s even bigger!
